Hourly since 2026-08-09: the daily cron had delivered zero runs in the workflow's entire history — all ten were workflow_dispatch — so an external answer arrived only when a lap happened to have MCP tools, and that is the lane the whole route depends on. 2026-08-10: the pool this row calls separate and unused is actually TWO weekly windows, and only one was reachable — codex exec with no --model runs the account default, so GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark stayed at 100% for this lane's entire history while being cited as spare capacity. The dispatch now names a model derived from the meter (scripts/spark-model.mjs) and falls back to the default if refused; scripts/spark-model.mjs --check runs in pulse.yml so it cannot quietly go back to unnamed.

liveness.note: Moved off state/answers/latest.json when the cron went hourly. That file only moves when a question is actually put to the model, and a healthy hourly lane skips most of its runs because the task already carries its done marker — so keyed on the answer, an idle lane and a stopped lane look the same. scripts/record-lane-run.mjs stamps checked_at on every run including the skips, which is the mark that dates the SCHEDULE rather than the product.

reconciliation_gap_nobody_has_closed: The reservation that dominates pacing — youtube-loop and cookie-daily at a derived upper bound each, capped to 16.80% — rests on rows only an MCP lap can verify. Between MCP laps the scheduler can change and nothing here would know. Actions cannot see it. Nobody has priced a workaround, and this line exists so the next lap does not rediscover the gap as if it were new.
